section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 1. Introduction
text:
# SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle  
## 1. Introduction  
This handbook defines the mandatory gates and practices for all software and data-flow related systems.

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 2. Requirements Phase > 2.1 Security Requirements Elicitation
text:
## 2. Requirements Phase  
### 2.1 Security Requirements Elicitation  
All systems that process sensitive data must identify trust boundaries and external entities during the requirements phase.

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 3. Design Phase > 3.1 Architecture Review Gate
text:
## 3. Design Phase  
### 3.1 Architecture Review Gate  
Before implementation begins, a formal Architecture Review must be completed. The review shall examine:  
- All data flows that cross trust boundaries
- Classification of data stores
- Authentication and authorization of external entities

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 3. Design Phase > 3.1 Architecture Review Gate > 3.1.1 Trust Boundary Analysis
text:
#### 3.1.1 Trust Boundary Analysis  
Every data flow that crosses a trust boundary requires explicit documentation of the protection mechanisms in place. Unprotected flows are prohibited.

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 3. Design Phase > 3.1 Architecture Review Gate > 3.1.2 External Entity Controls
text:
#### 3.1.2 External Entity Controls  
External entities must be authenticated and authorized according to the principle of least privilege. Direct write access from external entities to internal data stores is forbidden without an intermediate process.

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 4. Implementation Phase > 4.1 Secure Coding Standards
text:
## 4. Implementation Phase  
### 4.1 Secure Coding Standards  
Implementation must follow the approved secure coding checklist. Data flow related controls from the Design Phase remain mandatory.

section: SDLC Handbook – Secure Development Lifecycle > 5. Verification Phase > 5.1 Security Testing Gate
text:
## 5. Verification Phase  
### 5.1 Security Testing Gate  
All DFDs and implemented flows must be re-validated against the original Architecture Review findings.

section: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls > SEC-DFD-001 – Trust Boundary Definition
text:
# Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls  
## SEC-DFD-001 – Trust Boundary Definition  
Every system must explicitly identify and document all trust boundaries. A trust boundary exists wherever data or control passes between entities of different trust levels.  
**Risk Tier:** Critical
**SDLC Phase:** Design
heading_path: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls

section: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls > SEC-DFD-014 – External Entity Access
text:
## SEC-DFD-014 – External Entity Access  
External entities shall not have direct write access to internal data stores. All such access must be mediated by an authenticated and authorized process.  
**Risk Tier:** Critical
**SDLC Phase:** Design, Implementation
heading_path: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls

section: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls > SEC-DFD-022 – Data Store Classification
text:
## SEC-DFD-022 – Data Store Classification  
All data stores must be classified according to data sensitivity. Classification drives encryption, access control, and monitoring requirements.  
**Risk Tier:** High
**SDLC Phase:** Requirements, Design
heading_path: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls

section: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls > SEC-DFD-031 – Data Flow Integrity
text:
## SEC-DFD-031 – Data Flow Integrity  
Data flows that cross trust boundaries must provide integrity protection (e.g., TLS, message authentication) appropriate to the risk tier of the data.  
**Risk Tier:** High
**SDLC Phase:** Design, Implementation
heading_path: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls

section: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls > SEC-DFD-045 – Process Isolation
text:
## SEC-DFD-045 – Process Isolation  
Processes that handle data from different trust levels should be isolated unless a formal risk acceptance is recorded.  
**Risk Tier:** Medium
**SDLC Phase:** Design, Implementation
heading_path: Technical Security Baseline – Data Flow & Trust Controls
